title: Trump Asked to Participate in Oil Production, but I Told Him It Can’t Be Done, Sheinbaum Says
author: Sugeyry Romina Gándara
content:
_This article by[Sugeyry Romina
Gándara](https://www.sinembargo.mx/author/sugeyry_gandara/) originally
appeared in the [October 19, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4889925/trump-pidio-participar-en-
produccion-de-petroleo-pero-le-dije-que-no-se-puede-csp/), an independent
Mexican digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, October 19 (SinEmbargo).—** **President[Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo
(CSP)](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/claudia-sheinbaum/)** revealed that her
counterpart **Donald Trump** has asked her during their phone conversations to
increase purchases of US **natural gas**. However, the Mexican president
explained that she has rejected the proposal, given that the country plans to
increase the extraction of this fuel on national territory.

At her morning press conference, she also explained that the Republican leader
has expressed interest in having companies from his country intervene in
**oil** production in **Mexico**. In this regard, she maintained that there
are constitutional and legal restrictions that prevent granting rights over
**hydrocarbons** , although she clarified that US companies can expand their
participation through contracts with **[Petróleos Mexicanos
(Pemex)](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/pemex/)**.

> He has raised at times whether he can help, that is how he puts it, in oil
> production, and in every case we have been clear. I have told him: ‘Look,
> President Trump, here there is a Constitution and here there are laws. So
> here oil rights cannot be granted.’
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

In this context, she recalled that US companies have participated for decades
in activities of the Mexican oil industry as Pemex contractors, so that route
would allow them to expand their involvement without modifying the legal
framework that regulates the national energy sector.

## Trump Does Not Condition USMCA on Handing Over “Narco-Politicians”

The Chief Executive denied that the occupant of the White House is
conditioning the negotiation of a trade agreement with Mexico on the handover
of politicians allegedly linked to drug trafficking or on actions against
corruption. She also clarified that the US president has not used the term
“narco-politicians” during their phone conversations.

> “None of that, none of that. And besides, what narco-politicians? No, no,
> none of that,” she responded when asked about the issue.

On the other hand, she acknowledged that Trump has told her that there are
areas of Mexican territory controlled by criminal organizations, a claim she
has directly rejected. According to her account, she has responded that this
situation does not correspond to the country’s reality and has presented him
with the results of her security strategy.

![Claudia Sheinbaum gestures during her morning press
conference](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/2026-10-19-trump-oil-sinembargo-02.jpg)The President
called for separating the bilateral relationship from US electoral disputes.
Photo: Camila Ayala Benabib, Cuartoscuro

> “Well, that is not true, President. What’s more, look at the results we
> have. Fentanyl crossings have been reduced by 60-some percent, we cut the
> number of homicides in half. Various results that have been achieved in
> security. If that were true, well, we obviously would not have these
> results,” she stated.

The president attributed part of the statements about Mexico to the electoral
context of the neighboring country and maintained that these are US opinions.
For that reason, she again asked that the Nation not be used as a political
campaign issue.
